body.en: The imaginary unit \( i \) extends the reals; complex numbers add, multiply, and have a modulus and conjugate.
\( i^{2}=-1 \); \( z=a+bi \) has modulus \( |z|=\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}} \) and conjugate \( \bar{z}=a-bi \), with \( z\bar{z}=|z|^{2} \).

Write \(z=-1+\sqrt{3}\,i\) in modulus-argument form and find \(z^4\) using De Moivre's theorem.

\(|z|=\sqrt{1+3}=2\). \(\arg z=\pi-\arctan\sqrt{3}=\pi-\tfrac{\pi}{3}=\tfrac{2\pi}{3}\).

\(z=2\bigl(\cos\tfrac{2\pi}{3}+i\sin\tfrac{2\pi}{3}\bigr)\). By De Moivre: \(z^4=2^4\bigl(\cos\tfrac{8\pi}{3}+i\sin\tfrac{8\pi}{3}\bigr)=16\bigl(\cos\tfrac{2\pi}{3}+i\sin\tfrac{2\pi}{3}\bigr)=16(-\tfrac{1}{2}+\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}i)=-8+8\sqrt3\,i\).

question.en: Given that \(z_1=3+4i\) and \(z_2=1-2i\), find \(\dfrac{z_1}{z_2}\) in the form \(a+bi\).

label.en: ⚠️ Cambridge 9709 Traps — Principal Argument Interval & Geometric Loci

body.en:
Principal Argument Range: Cambridge 9709 requires the principal argument to satisfy \(-\pi < \arg(z) \le \pi\). When \(z\) lies in Quadrant 2 (\(x < 0, y > 0\)), \(\arg(z) = \pi - \arctan(|y/x|)\). In Quadrant 3 (\(x < 0, y < 0\)), \(\arg(z) = -(\pi - \arctan(|y/x|))\). Blindly using \(\arctan(y/x)\) on a calculator yields the wrong quadrant.

Standard Geometric Loci:

  • \(|z - z_1| = r\): Circle of radius \(r\) centred at \(z_1\).
  • \(|z - z_1| = |z - z_2|\): Perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining \(z_1\) and \(z_2\).
  • \(\arg(z - z_1) = \alpha\): Half-line starting from (but not including) \(z_1\) at angle \(\alpha\) to the positive real direction.

question.en: On an Argand diagram, the point \(P\) represents the complex number \(z\) such that \(|z - (2 + 3i)| \le 2\). Find the greatest possible value of \(|z|\) for points in this region.

solution.en:
The locus \(|z - (2 + 3i)| \le 2\) represents a circular disc of radius \(R = 2\) with center at \(C(2, 3)\).

The distance from the origin \(O(0, 0)\) to the center \(C\) is:

\[|C| = \sqrt{2^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{4 + 9} = \sqrt{13} \approx 3.6055\]

The point on the disc farthest from the origin lies on the line passing through \(O\) and \(C\), on the far boundary of the circle:

\[|z|_{\max} = |C| + R = \sqrt{13} + 2 \approx 3.606 + 2 = 5.61\text{ (3 s.f.)}\]
